actions.label: Let existing guard structures organize and implement distribution
Commit to stop diverting food and distribute equally to all refugees
Seek government funding for guard pay and generator costs instead of using FWB food
Provide guard security and escort at distribution points while FWB conducts handout
Maintain perimeter security and screening during distribution
Prioritize local hiring and local actors in camp activities
Permit FWB nutritional assessments under camp security coordination
Grant FWB staff escorted, coordinated camp access managed by camp administration
Provide food rations to guards and their families as compensation
Deliver an ongoing, regular supply of food aid to the camp
Accept prior coordination and guard escort at all times, without unrestricted movement in the camp
Conduct donor-required nutritional assessments in a security-safe way agreed with the camp

goals.label: Host community economy and goodwill toward the camp
Nutritional assessments and documentation meet donor requirements
Camp generators and power keep running
Camp guard/militia structures control food distribution
Camp receives a steady ongoing supply of food aid
Commander's authority and appearance of strength
Control of camp information and assessments
FWB controls and oversees food distribution
FWB neutrality and not supporting armed actors
Food aid diverted by guards or militia
Guards and their families are fed and compensated
Refugees stay contained in the camp rather than reaching the capital
Safety of FWB staff and local assistants
Government funding and resources for camp operations
Senior Militia Leader's approval of the commander
Terrorists or hostile actors inside the camp are contained
Working relationship with MASHA and local partners

redLines.label: Allow FWB and its chosen local assistants to manage food disbursement
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Have FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants manage food disbursement

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
